newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Royale Belge says no decision on future.
newsitem.headline: Royale Belge says no decision on future.

text.p: Royale Belge chairman Jean-Pierre de Launoit said on Wednesday that no decision had yet been taken concerning the company's future following the merger of French parent AXA-UAP.

"Since December, there have been studies in different parts of the group to see whether there should be a bringing together of the units in which AXA-UAP holds interests...today these studies are not finished and they are continuing in a harmonious way," de Launoit told the annual shareholders meeting.
"Whatever the solution is, it must favour the development of Royale Belge in line with the fundamental interests...of shareholders," de Launoit said.
Royale Belge is owned 51.2 percent by holding company Royale Vendome, an investment vehicle 49.9 percent held by Compagnie UAP which is held for 91.5 percent by AXA-UAP.
Belgian holding company Groupe Bruxelles Lambert (GBL) has a key 25.1 percent stake in Royale Vendome.
Belgian Sofina with 3.8 percent and Compagnie Nationale a Portefeuille (CNP/NPM) with 2.7 percent are also among Royale Belge's shareholders.

There has been intense speculation on the Brussels bourse in recent sessions that Royale Belge, and its 12.4 percent stake in bank BBL, were about to be sold, possibly to Dutch ING. ING has declined to comment.
A Royale Belge sale to ING would leave the Dutch group incontestably in control of BBL -- something it first aimed for in 1992 but failed to achieve.
